name: Intercom Support, governed - contacts, conversations, replies
description: Intercom API actions for AI agents.

commands.title: List Intercom Contacts
commands.description: Fetches a paginated list of all contacts (users and leads). Max 150 per page. Use starting_after cursor to get the next page. Read-only.

per_page.description: The number of items returned in a single response. Default is 20, max is 150.

starting_after.description: The cursor used for pagination. Extract this value from the `pages.next.starting_after` field of the previous API response.

commands.title: Create a new Intercom contact
commands.description: Creates a new user or lead in Intercom. Requires at least one identifier: email, external_id, or role. Returns the created contact object with id and attributes.

role.description: The role of the contact, (pass one option of the list: [lead, user]).

external_id.description: A unique identifier for the contact which is given to Intercom

email_verified.description: Whether the contact's email address has been verified. Set to true to indicate you have verified the contact owns this email address, or false to mark it as unverified. Must be supplied together with an email in the same request; sending it without an email returns a 400.

avatar.description: An image URL containing the avatar of a contact

signed_up_at.description: (Unix timestamp in seconds) The time specified for when a contact signed up.

last_seen_at.description: (Unix timestamp in seconds) The time when the contact was last seen (either where the Intercom Messenger was installed or when specified manually).

owner_id.description: The id of an admin that has been assigned account ownership of the contact

unsubscribed_from_emails.description: Whether the contact is unsubscribed from emails

custom_attributes.description: Custom attributes for the contact. Values may be strings, numbers, booleans, arrays, or nested objects.

commands.title: Get a contact by its id
commands.description: Fetches a single contact by ID. If the contact was merged into another, requesting it returns HTTP 410 Gone with a Link header pointing to the canonical contact.

include_merge_history.description: (query url parameter); Pass `true` to include the contact's merge history in the response. Only returned for contacts with a `user` role.

commands.title: Delete a contact by its id
commands.description: Permanently deletes a single contact by its ID. Warning: Intercom deletions are permanent and cannot be undone.

contact_id.description: The Intercom ID of the contact to delete.

commands.title: Update a contact by its id
commands.description: Updates an existing Intercom contact by ID. Provide only the fields you want to change. At least one updatable field is required.

contact_id.description: The Intercom ID of the contact to update.

include_merge_history.description: (query url parameter); Pass `true` to include the contact's merge history in the response. Only returned for contacts with a `user` role.

role.description: The role of the contact, (pass one option of the list: [lead, user]).

external_id.description: A unique identifier for the contact which is given to Intercom

email_verified.description: Whether the contact's email address has been verified. Set to true to indicate you have verified the contact owns this email address, or false to mark it as unverified. Must be supplied together with an email in the same request; sending it without an email returns a 400.

avatar.description: An image URL containing the avatar of a contact

signed_up_at.description: (Unix timestamp in seconds) The time specified for when a contact signed up.

last_seen_at.description: (Unix timestamp in seconds) The time when the contact was last seen (either where the Intercom Messenger was installed or when specified manually).

owner_id.description: The id of an admin that has been assigned account ownership of the contact

unsubscribed_from_emails.description: Whether the contact is unsubscribed from emails

custom_attributes.description: Custom attributes for the contact. Values may be strings, numbers, booleans, arrays, or nested objects.

commands.title: Merge a lead and a user
commands.description: Merges a lead contact into a user contact. The lead contact is permanently destroyed and cannot be recovered. Provide skip_duplicate_validation='true' if the contacts share no matching email or phone.

from.description: The unique identifier for the contact to merge away from. Must be a lead.

into.description: The unique identifier for the contact to merge into. Must be a user.

skip_duplicate_validation.description: Set to `true` to merge two contacts that are not duplicates (they share no matching email or phone).

include_merge_history.description: (query url parameter); Pass `true` to include the merge history of the resulting contact in the response. Only returned for contacts with a `user` role.

commands.title: List all conversations
commands.description: Fetches a paginated list of all conversations. Use the `starting_after` cursor from the previous response to fetch subsequent pages.

per_page.description: The number of items returned in a single response. Default is 20, max is 150.

starting_after.description: The cursor used for pagination. Extract this value from the `pages.next.starting_after` field of the previous API response.

commands.title: Delete a conversation by its id.
commands.description: Permanently deletes a single conversation. If `retain_metrics=true` (default), reporting data is kept. If `retain_metrics=false`, all reporting data is also deleted (requires `delete_conversations_and_metrics` OAuth scope).

conversation_id.description: conversation id should be integer number

retain_metrics.description: Pass 'true' (default) to delete the conversation while retaining reporting data. Pass 'false' to delete the conversation and all associated reporting data (requires `delete_conversations_and_metrics` scope).

commands.title: Fetches a conversation by its id.
commands.description: You can fetch the details of a single conversation.This will return a single Conversation model with all its conversation parts.

conversation_id.description: conversation id should be integer number

display_as.description: Set to plaintext to retrieve conversation messages in plain text. This affects both the body and subject fields. Inline links are rendered as `label (url)`, preserving the link URL alongside the visible text.

include_translations.description: If set to true, conversation parts will be translated to the detected language of the conversation.

commands.title: Creates a conversation.
commands.description:
You can create a conversation that has been initiated by a contact (ie. user or lead).
The conversation can be an in-app message only.

from_type.description: The role associated, one value of: [lead, user, contact].

from_id.description: The identifier for the contact which is given by Intercom, should be uuid formatted with length 24.

body.description: The content of the message. HTML is not supported.

subject.description: The title of the email. Only applicable if the message type is email.

attachment_urls.description: A list of image URLs that will be added as attachments. You can include up to 10 URLs.

created_at.description: The time the conversation was created as a UTC Unix timestamp. If not provided, the current time will be used. Example: 1671028894.

brand_id.description: The unique identifier of the brand to associate with this conversation. Example: '123'.

commands.title: Update a conversation.
commands.description: You can update an existing conversation. This endpoint handles both conversation updates and custom object associations.

conversation_id.description: The id of the conversation to target, should be integer.

display_as.description: Set to 'plaintext' to retrieve conversation messages in plain text.

read.description: Pass 'true' to mark the conversation as read.

title.description: The title given to the conversation.

custom_attributes.description: Key-value pairs of custom attributes to attach. Example: {"paid_subscriber": true, "monthly_spend": 155.5}. Note: Workspace must not have duplicate custom attribute names.

company_id.description: The unique Intercom ID of the company to associate. Set to null to remove.

commands.title: Reply to a conversation.
commands.description: You can reply to a conversation with a message from an admin or on behalf of a contact, or with a note for admins, if you set type = 'user', then exactly one field of [intercom_user_id, email, user_id] should be provided, otherwise if you set type = 'admin' then you have to provide only 'admin_id'.

conversation_id.description: The ID of the conversation to reply to.

message_type.description: 'comment' (visible to user) or 'note' (internal team note), if type = 'admin' then message_type accepts ['comment' or 'note'], otherwise type = 'user' accepts only 'note' .

type.description: 'admin' or 'user'. Who is sending the reply.

admin_id.description: The ID of the admin sending the reply. Required if type = 'admin'.

body.description: The text content of the reply, not required only when type = 'admin'.

attachment_urls.description: A list of image URLs that will be added as attachments. You can include up to 10 URLs.

intercom_user_id.description: The identifier for the contact as given by Intercom, only required when type = 'user'.

email.description: The email you have defined for the user, only required when type = 'user'.

user_id.description: The external_id you have defined for the contact, only required when type = 'user'.

commands.title: Identify admin
commands.description: View the currently authenticated admin along with workspace information.
